Plutarch, *Life of Theseus* 23.1: the Athenians kept the ship Theseus came home in, swapping each rotten timber for a new one, down to the time of Demetrius of Phalerum, so that philosophers argued whether it was still the same ship. Hobbes, *De Corpore* II.11.7, adds the twist: suppose someone kept all the old planks and rebuilt them. Now there are two ships; which one is Theseus's? My own version is Dad's hurley. "This is the hurley I won the 1979 Leinster under-14 final with." New bas in 1983, new handle in 1990, re-banded more times than he can count. He would fight anyone who said it wasn't the same hurley, and I've never had the heart to try. Used it with fifth years on 4 Feb 2025; the class split 15 to 11 in favour of "same hurley". Related: [[Gettier cases]] (another three-sentence puzzle that eats a whole class), [[Free will debate]] (if I'm a different set of cells every seven years, who's responsible for what I did at twenty?).
